reader.requirement: An UNSTRING delimiter, whether literal-1 or the content of identifier-2, may hold any character of the native character set (LOW-VALUE, HIGH-VALUE, QUOTE, SPACE, control characters and high-ordinal characters named by SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, punctuation, lower case), alone or in a multi-character delimiter, and each such delimiter is matched as written.

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry in StringUnstringBinder.cs and CobolStringOps.cs: the delimiter screens (SR1/SR2 category, ALL figurative, zero length) and the runtime's ordinal IndexOf matching take no edition; the one UNSTRING edition gate on the path is VersionConformancePass.VisitUnstringStatement's SR7 check.

reader.notes: The binder places no restriction on a delimiter's characters, and the runtime matches with ordinal string comparison, so any character of the set, printable or not, delimits. The seed sites (PictureAnalyzer, CobolEdit) do not implement this rule; the implementation is StringUnstringBinder.BindUnstring and CobolStringOps.UnstringExtract.
